verses.verse:
तत्र वर्णाश्च चत्वारः कथ्यन्ते हि मनीषिभिः।
स्थाय्यारोह्यवरोही च संचारीति यथाक्रमाः।९७।
verses.text: There, the wise speak of four varṇas (kinds of melodic movement): sthāyī (steady), ārohī (ascending), avarohī (descending) and sañcārī (wandering), in that order.

commentary.text: Just as the four states of stability, rise, decline and busyness give a person many forms and titles, so in the notes, on the basis of the actions of steadiness, climbing, descending and moving about, various groups of notes and tunes arise. A group that is bound to tāla (metric cycle) is called a dhun (tune) or gīt (song). A group that is small and bound only to laya (tempo) we call an alaṅkāra (patterned exercise). Now, there are many texts for the definition of laya and tāla, so after giving a brief introduction to them we will move on to alaṅkāra.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
